bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/observable.rs (bifrost_app::observable::Observable), springboard/ui/src/observe.rs (Observable<T>), springboard/sdk/src/process_info.rs (change observers); springboard/sdk/src/observable.rs (with_observation_tracking, Observations), springboard/sdk/src/observable_object.rs (observable_model!)
summary: BifrOSt has manual value observation: an Observable<T> that notifies subscribers only when the value changes, with Combine-style sink, map and remove_duplicates. A set made inside a subscriber is queued and delivered in order, and cancelling a subscriber during a change sticks. with_observation_tracking records the observables a closure reads and fires one on-change callback; Observable::observations pulls changes in order. A declarative observable_model! macro gives a model struct with one change publisher, so a property write notifies the owner. It still has no derive, no tracking options or tokens, no continuous observation, and no async sequence.

features.note: Declarative macro: observable_model! { struct Name { field: T = init } } gives a struct whose fields are Observable<T>, all linked to one ObservableObject publisher. No derive, so no per-property opt-out (ObservationIgnored) and no computed properties. Built on parity/team-a-09; not yet verified on Midget.

features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/observable.rs (Observable::set, update, subscribe, sink); springboard/ui/src/observe.rs (Observable<T>::set, subscribe(old, new))
features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 23 tests. Notifies only when the value differs (PartialEq) in the UI-model copy; the SDK copy notifies on every set. A set made from inside a subscriber is queued and delivered after the running change, in order (fixed in SDK, was dropped). Cancelling another subscriber during a change is now durable. UI-model copy (ui/src/observe.rs) is unchanged: its subscribers receive old and new values only.

verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 23 tests. with_observation_tracking(apply, on_change) records each Observable read by get() inside apply and calls on_change once when one changes; the tracking then ends. Apple's withObservationTracking returns only the closure value and also covers options, and its onChange runs before the change; here on_change runs after the change, and reads inside on_change are not tracked. Only the SDK Observable is tracked; the UI-model copy is not.

verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 23 tests. Pull-based sequence of the changes after the call, oldest first; dropping it stops recording. It is the synchronous counterpart of Apple's Observations: it has no suspension, no AsyncSequence conformance and no withContinuousObservation(options:apply:).
verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 23 tests. Subscription cancels on drop (AnyCancellable). No event or options types for tracking.
Macro-only behaviour of the Swift language; with no macro in BifrOSt there is nothing to mark.

features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 4 tests. Observer-style subscriptions exist for system events (NotificationCenter, workspace, thermal state, Low Power Mode). They are not Observation's property-level tracking.

gaps: No derive for the @Observable macro: model properties are listed in observable_model!, and there is no per-property opt-out. with_observation_tracking tracks only SDK Observable reads.
No withContinuousObservation(options:apply:), ObservationTracking.Options, Event or Token: with_observation_tracking is one-shot and returns only the closure value.
Observations is pull-based (try_next), not an AsyncSequence; there is no executor or suspension in the pure std model.
docs/bifrost-ui.md:1435 still describes the old re-entrant set limit; that shared doc is out of scope for this change and is listed for a later update.
SwiftUI-style integration (view invalidation from observed model state) not verified in code; no binding found in this pass.
